PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 79 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 09/10/27 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of persistent edema, and reassessment of mental health treatment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for a follow-up visit approximately six weeks after his last appointment. He reports a slight improvement in his respiratory symptoms since the last visit, attributing this to the increased dosage of fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler, which he now utilizes at 2 puffs twice daily. However, he continues to rely on his albuterol inhaler approximately five to six times a day, especially during episodes of increased physical activity. He expresses ongoing concern regarding his dyspnea, particularly with exertion, and notes that he still experiences nocturnal wheezing.
Despite these improvements, Mr. Fairfax's bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant issue. He describes the edema as persistently at a 3+ pitting level and states that it has not improved despite dietary sodium restrictions and adherence to his furosemide regimen (120 mg daily). He expresses frustration over how the edema limits his mobility and affects his quality of life, particularly with daily activities.
In terms of his mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports that he continues to benefit from cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). He notes that his anxiety levels have stabilized somewhat but still experiences occasional spikes in anxiety related to his health status. He expresses a desire to explore additional coping strategies to manage these fluctuations.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + persistent dyspnea, + decreased nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + ongoing joint pain, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using five to six times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily (increased). 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 120 mg daily (unchanged). 7. Sertraline 100 mg daily.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 80, BP 128/75, RR 24, O2 sat 82% on room air
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but more engaged than prior visits. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.9, Hgb 10.5, Hct 31.5, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.2, Cl 100, CO2 28, BUN 30, Cr 1.8, Glucose 90 3. BNP: 600 (decreased). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.0 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax reports slight improvement in respiratory function with the increased fluticasone/salmeterol dosage. Continue current regimen and consider adding a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) for acute symptom relief. A follow-up pulmonary function test is advised in one month to assess lung function more accurately. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists despite the current furosemide dosage. Referral to nephrology remains recommended for further evaluation of renal function and potential adjustment of diuretic therapy. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions continues to be essential. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax reports benefits from CBT. Continue sertraline 100 mg daily. Follow-up with psychiatry in one month for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Discuss potential adjunctive therapies, such as mindfulness techniques, to help manage anxiety.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
